CDW.why: A technology leader one close from a new high, its averages lined up in order and a rising weekly trend.
CDW.contested: Contested: the hourly trigger has no volume test and part of the room wants the dip to the short-term average or the back-test of the broken level; it clears on a daily close over the pivot on heavy volume.

EXLS.why: A technology leader that has just closed through its pivot with its averages in order, waiting for the break to show buyers.
EXLS.contested: Contested: the break printed on very light volume and the force reading is unresolved; it clears on a daily close over the pivot on heavy volume, or the force reading turning back up first.

PCOR.why: A technology leader at its yearly closing high just under its pivot, with strong relative strength and light volume.
PCOR.contested: Contested: the price is already far above value after a steep run, so part of the room wants the dip to the short-term average; it clears on that pullback or a daily close over the pivot on heavy volume.

EMBJ.why: An industrials leader with its averages in order, resting under its recent swing high in the one sector still entering.
EMBJ.contested: Contested: the trigger is a breakout entry and part of the room buys only the pullback to the short-term average; it clears on that pullback, and the price must first reset under the too-late line.

SN.why: A consumer leader with top-tier relative strength resting just under its yearly high, its averages in order.
SN.contested: Contested: the trend has already left value, so part of the room buys only the dip to the short-term average or a reclaim of the two-week volume line; it clears on that dip and reclaim.

BBY.why: A consumer leader with its averages in order, just above its pivot on light volume, with earnings next week.
BBY.contested: Contested: the trigger chases a fresh break, and part of the room wants the test of the broken level or the pullback to the short-term average; it clears on a dip under the broken level and an hourly close back above it.

CHYM.why: A financial leader with top-tier relative strength and its averages in order, already well past its pivot.
CHYM.contested: Rejected: the hourly trigger buys an extension, not a pause or a new closing high; it would change on a pullback to the short-term average and an hourly close back above it.

BTSG.why: A healthcare leader sitting at its pivot with its averages in order, slated as a buy before the quality check.
BTSG.contested: Rejected: the hourly trigger carries no volume test on a light-volume break; it would change on a daily close over Friday's high on heavy volume.

COLD.why: A real estate leader at its yearly high on rising volume, slated as a watch for a dip to value.
COLD.contested: Rejected: the trigger rests an order inside the dip instead of buying the turn or the new high; it would change on an hourly close back above the short-term average after a dip.

RBRK.why: A held long carried into the room to ask the add question; no case to add was filed.
RBRK.contested: Not slated: no analyst filed a case for it at cross-examination, so the hold rests on the broker stop.

SPCX.why: A held short carried into the room; one case for it survived cross-examination.
SPCX.contested: Not slated: the room did not carry it to the slate, so the only line is the live broker buy stop.
